products.overview: Most gas analysis starts with a calibration curve, built and rebuilt for every compound you need to track. OMEGA 5 skips that step. OPUS GA software quantifies more than 350 compounds directly, by continuously tracking gas pressure and temperature during analysis and correcting for both in real time. A 5-meter multi-reflection gas cell, heatable to 191°C, sits inside a 19-inch rackmount housing. The TE-MCT detector needs no liquid nitrogen, so measurement runs continuously. Standard resolution reaches better than 2 cm⁻¹, with an option to push past 1 cm⁻¹ for gas mixtures where signals overlap. Pressure handling runs from 2 bar standard up to 15 bar with the high-pressure option, and DryPath removes the need for external purge gas entirely.
features: Calibration-Free Quantification: OPUS GA tracks pressure and temperature continuously and quantifies over 350 compounds without a calibration curve.
5-Meter Multi-Reflection Gas Cell: Heatable to 191°C, delivering the path length needed for sensitive detection.
TE-MCT Detector: Runs continuously with no liquid nitrogen requirement, for uninterrupted measurement.
High-Resolution Option: Pushes spectral resolution past 1 cm⁻¹, for gas mixtures with significant signal overlap.
High-Pressure Option: Handles measurements up to 15 bar absolute, suited to trace impurity detection and elevated-pressure processes.
Stabilized H2O and CO2 Background: A sealed, purgeable optics compartment holds background levels stable, reaching limits as low as 10 ppm for H2O.
DryPath Purge-Free Operation: Removes the need for external purge gas, extending OMEGA 5 to mobile applications.
RockSolid Interferometer and CenterGlow IR Source: Vibration-resistant, long-life core optics built for years of maintenance-free data acquisition.

faqs.question: What is the OMEGA 5 FT-IR Gas Analyzer used for?
faqs.answer: OMEGA 5 monitors gas concentrations in real time, quantifying over 350 compounds without calibration, across industrial process monitoring, environmental analysis, and trace impurity detection.

faqs.question: How does calibration-free quantification actually work?
faqs.answer: OPUS GA software continuously records the gas's pressure and temperature during analysis and corrects for both in real time, which is what allows accurate quantification without a calibration curve.

faqs.question: How do I decide between standard and high-resolution configuration?
faqs.answer: Choose standard resolution, better than 2 cm⁻¹, for gas mixtures with clearly separated IR signals, and the high-resolution option, better than 1 cm⁻¹, when your mixture has significant signal overlap that needs to be resolved.

faqs.question: How do I decide if I need the high-pressure option?
faqs.answer: Choose the high-pressure option, up to 15 bar absolute, when you're detecting trace impurities or measuring gas directly at elevated industrial process pressure rather than after depressurizing it.

faqs.question: What is the H2O detection limit on the OMEGA 5?
faqs.answer: As low as 10 ppm, achieved through a sealed, purgeable optics compartment that stabilizes background H2O and CO2 levels.

faqs.question: Does the OMEGA 5 need liquid nitrogen?
faqs.answer: No. The TE-MCT detector runs continuously without a cryogen requirement.

faqs.question: What is DryPath, and when should I use it?
faqs.answer: DryPath is an optional feature that eliminates the need for external purge gas, which is worth adding wherever purge gas supply is inconvenient or unavailable, including mobile applications.

faqs.question: Can the OMEGA 5 be used for mobile gas analysis?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the DryPath option, which removes the external purge gas requirement that would otherwise limit it to fixed installations.

faqs.question: How long is the gas cell, and can it be heated?
faqs.answer: The multi-reflection gas cell is 5 meters, heatable up to 191°C.

faqs.question: What is the price of the OMEGA 5 FT-IR Gas Analyzer in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the resolution, pressure, and DryPath options your application needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your gas mixture and operating conditions are confirmed.

sections.subheading: No calibration curve, and a real mechanism behind that claim
body: OPUS GA continuously tracks gas pressure and temperature during analysis and corrects for both, which is what makes quantifying over 350 compounds without calibration actually work.
A long path length in a compact footprint. The 5-meter multi-reflection gas cell, heatable to 191°C, fits inside a standard 19-inch rackmount housing.
No liquid nitrogen, no interruption. The TE-MCT detector runs continuously, without the downtime a cryogen-dependent detector would require.
Resolution scales to the mixture. Standard resolution reaches better than 2 cm⁻¹; the high-resolution option pushes past 1 cm⁻¹ for gas mixtures with heavily overlapping signals.
Pressure handling goes well beyond atmospheric. The high-pressure option reaches 15 bar absolute, suited to detecting trace impurities and running industrial measurements under real process pressure.

Background drift is engineered out, not corrected for after the fact. A sealed, purgeable optics compartment holds H2O and CO2 background levels stable, reaching quantification limits as low as 10 ppm for H2O.
It can leave the rack behind entirely. The optional DryPath feature removes the need for external purge gas, opening up mobile applications the standard configuration can't reach.

Confirmed solution: Bruker OMEGA 5 FT-IR Gas Analyzer. Standard: better than 2 cm⁻¹ resolution, up to 2 bar operating pressure. Optional: better than 1 cm⁻¹ resolution, up to 15 bar operating pressure, DryPath purge-free operation. Full physical specifications (dimensions beyond rackmount format, weight, power) are available on request from Inkarp.

sections.eyebrow: Spectral Resolution, Pressure and Detection Limits
sections.title: Matching the standard or upgraded configuration to your gas mixture
body: Two configuration choices decide what OMEGA 5 can actually see in a gas sample: how finely it resolves overlapping signals, and how much pressure it can measure under.

Standard resolution, better than 2 cm⁻¹, handles most routine gas analysis cleanly. Where compounds share closely overlapping IR signals, the high-resolution option pushes past 1 cm⁻¹, separating what the standard configuration would blur together. Pressure works the same way: standard operation covers up to 2 bar absolute, while the high-pressure option reaches 15 bar, which matters both for trace impurity detection and for measuring gas directly at real industrial process pressure rather than after it's been stepped down.
